events.title: 절강 해녕에서 태어나다
events.description: 절강성 해녕에서 태어났다. 자는 정안이며, 만년에는 호를 관당이라 했다.
events.description_en: He was born in Haining, Zhejiang. His courtesy name was Jing'an, and in his later years he went by the sobriquet Guantang.

events.title: 나진옥의 동문학사에 들어가다
events.title_en: He joined Luo Zhenyu's Eastern Literature Society
events.description: 상하이에서 나진옥이 세운 동문학사에 들어가 서양 학문과 외국어를 익혔다. 이때 맺은 나진옥과의 인연이 평생 학문의 동반자 관계로 이어졌다.
events.description_en: In Shanghai he joined the Eastern Literature Society founded by Luo Zhenyu, where he studied Western learning and foreign languages. The bond he formed with Luo there grew into a lifelong scholarly partnership.

events.title: 나진옥의 도움으로 일본에 유학하다
events.title_en: He studied in Japan with Luo Zhenyu's support
events.description: 나진옥의 재정 지원으로 도쿄물리학교에 들어가 낮에는 영어를, 밤에는 수학을 배웠다. 영양 부족으로 각기병을 얻어 이듬해 봄 학업을 접고 돌아왔다.
events.description_en: With Luo Zhenyu's financial backing he entered the Tokyo Physical School, studying English by day and mathematics by night. Malnutrition brought on beriberi, and he had to give up his studies and return the following spring.

events.title: 쇼펜하우어의 눈으로 『홍루몽』을 읽다
events.title_en: He read Dream of the Red Chamber through Schopenhauer's eyes
events.description: 칸트와 쇼펜하우어의 철학을 파고들며 『홍루몽평론』을 썼다. 서양 미학으로 중국 소설을 읽어낸 첫 시도였다.
events.description_en: Deep in the study of Kant and Schopenhauer, he wrote a commentary on Dream of the Red Chamber. It was the first attempt to read a Chinese novel through Western aesthetics.

events.title: 베이징 학부 도서국에서 일하다
events.title_en: He worked in the Ministry of Education's library bureau
events.description: 베이징으로 올라가 학부 도서국의 편집·번역 일을 맡았다.
events.description_en: He moved to Beijing and took up editing and translation work at the Ministry of Education's library bureau.

events.title: 『인간사화』로 경계설을 세우다
events.title_en: He set out the theory of jingjie in Renjian Cihua
events.description: 『인간사화』를 발표해 경치와 감정이 하나로 녹아든 상태를 뜻하는 경계설을 내놓았다. 송사 비평의 틀을 새로 짰다.
events.description_en: He published Renjian Cihua, putting forward his theory of jingjie — the fused state of scenery and feeling in a poem. It reshaped the framework for criticizing Song-dynasty ci poetry.

events.title: 신해혁명을 피해 일본으로 망명하다
events.title_en: He fled to Japan after the Xinhai Revolution
events.description: 신해혁명이 터지자 청 왕조에 대한 의리를 지켜 나진옥과 함께 일본 교토로 망명했다. 그곳에서 갑골문과 고대 문자 연구에 몰두했다.
events.description_en: When the Xinhai Revolution broke out, he kept his loyalty to the Qing dynasty and fled to Kyoto, Japan, together with Luo Zhenyu. There he threw himself into the study of oracle bone script and other ancient writings.

events.title: 중국으로 돌아오다
events.description: 다섯 해의 일본 생활을 마치고 중국으로 돌아왔다.
events.description_en: After five years in Japan he returned to China.

events.title: 푸이의 부름으로 자금성에 들어가다
events.title_en: Summoned by Puyi, he entered the Forbidden City
events.description: 폐위된 어린 황제 푸이의 부름을 받아 자금성에서 남서방행주로 그를 가르쳤다.
events.description_en: At the summons of the deposed boy emperor Puyi, he entered the Forbidden City and served as a tutor in the South Library.

events.title: 군벌의 정변으로 푸이가 쫓겨나다
events.title_en: A warlord coup drove Puyi from the palace
events.description: 군벌 펑위샹의 정변으로 푸이가 자금성에서 쫓겨났다. 청 왕조에 대한 의리를 지켜온 그에게는 큰 충격이었다.
events.description_en: A coup led by the warlord Feng Yuxiang drove Puyi from the Forbidden City. For a man who had kept faith with the Qing dynasty, it was a heavy blow.

events.title: 칭화 국학연구원의 4대 도사가 되다
events.title_en: He became one of Tsinghua's Four Great Mentors
events.description: 칭화대학 국학연구원 교수로 초빙되어 량치차오, 천인커, 자오위안런과 함께 4대 도사로 불렸다.
events.description_en: He was invited to teach at Tsinghua University's Institute of Chinese Studies, where he became known, alongside Liang Qichao, Chen Yinke, and Zhao Yuanren, as one of its Four Great Mentors.

events.title: 곤명호에 몸을 던지다
events.title_en: He drowned himself in Kunming Lake
events.description: 이화원 곤명호에 몸을 던져 스스로 목숨을 끊었다. 「이 격변을 겪었으니 다시 욕을 볼 수는 없다」는 유서를 남겼다.
events.description_en: He drowned himself in Kunming Lake at the Summer Palace. His suicide note read, 'Having lived through this upheaval, I cannot bear further humiliation.'
